h: Making Your Private Swim Go Swimmingly
p: Private hire is a different beast from a public swim, and a little bit of preparation helps you squeeze every minute out of your slot. The clock usually starts when your session does, not when the last straggler has finally wrestled their way into a costume, so getting the kids changed quickly is half the battle. Swimming costumes on under clothes before you leave the house is an old parents' trick for a reason.

Have a think about who's in charge before you get there. With nobody else in the pool, the supervising is down to your group, so agree which grown-ups are keeping an eye on the water at any one time, especially with weaker swimmers. Armbands, swim vests and a float or two are worth bringing if you're not sure what's provided.

A themed party is easy to pull off when you've got the whole pool to yourselves. Mermaids, pirates, superheroes: a few pool-safe toys and a playlist (if music is allowed) can turn an ordinary swim into a proper event. For little ones learning to swim, a quiet private session is golden for building confidence without the splashing and noise of a busy public pool.
Afterwards, warm everyone up with a hot drink and a snack, because cold kids after swimming are grumpy kids.

Ross-on-Wye has a good choice of cafés and pubs around the Market House for a post-swim feed. If the weather clears, The Prospect gardens behind St Mary's Church give you a sweeping view over the river, and the riverside meadows down by Rope Walk are perfect for letting the kids run off whatever energy they've got left. Goodrich Castle is only a short hop away for another day.
